title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Mack Wilson is trending up in the Seahawks-week defense, Isaiah Adams and Jon Gaines are in a right guard battle, and a defender named Keaton is on IR for at least four weeks.
summary: LaFleur said the defender placed on IR (transcribed as Keaton, who doesn't match the roster) is out at least four weeks, and the team will reevaluate after that and turn to the next man up. Max Melton sat the final stretch of the game and will be limited this week but is expected to be fine. Isaiah Adams is healthy enough to practice and will be reevaluated daily; LaFleur praised his camp and first series against Vegas, though he also got rolled up in practice. The right guard job is open: LaFleur praised Jon Gaines and said the Sunday starter will go to whoever gives the best chance to move the football, and he declined to say whether it is a health or competition call. LaFleur said the offense was slow in operation and left points out there, especially in the red zone, and the run game needs better combinations. He called Mack Wilson's play heavy and confident, noting he has been playing more instinctively since returning in late July. He also praised Simi Fehoko's block that earned him the NFC special teams honor. On Seattle, he called their defense the best he has seen with no weakness, said Drew Lock is a good quarterback who won't be rattled, and said the Seahawks look the same as last year's group.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 2 Media Availability | Wednesday, September 16th | Press Conference
headline: Falcons QB picture still unsettled for Sunday vs. Carolina: Tua (not practicing today) and Michael Penix Jr. (returning) are both in the mix, with the decision coming day to day, while Bijan Robinson's touch volume may drop.
summary: Stefanski opened by previewing Sunday's home opener against Carolina, praising Dave Canales and his staff and calling the Panthers a sound team with a strong quarterback, multiple outside receivers, a tough run game, and a big front. He said the defensive challenge starts with blocking that front, and he called special teams coordinator Tracy Smith outstanding. On quarterback, he said no decision has been made and nobody is ruled out: Tua Tagovailoa will not practice today but is improving, while Cooper Rush and Michael Penix Jr. will practice. He described the QB decision as day to day and said the team will work through it, declining to give specifics on Penix's practice reps but saying he is progressing and cleared like everyone else. Stefanski said Rush is still getting treatment on his back and will be a full participant, and that Jack Strand is not being ruled out for the game and fits well in the meeting room. He admitted Rush did not play well in last week's loss, but said there are lessons and that Rush is a veteran who will improve with reps. On Bijan Robinson, he said the 29-touch workload may not be sustainable every week, though Robinson wants the ball, and that spreading touches across the offense makes him harder to defend. He also said the team needs to get better as a group and praised a veteran for a strong locker-room presence.

title: Dave Canales:  'We're focused on consistency heading into Atlanta'

summary: Canales said the team had a good first full Wednesday back on the grass, focusing on fundamentals and on building on what is working. He expects Jalen Coker to play Sunday: Coker got an extended warm-up, a few snaps in team work, and treatment, with a bigger workload planned Thursday and a full practice cut loose Friday. Canales said Jimmy Horn Jr. was waived for roster reasons, not performance, and is expected to return to the practice squad. John Metchie III gets the opportunity to take on return duties and some of Coker's reps, which Canales said Bryce Young trusts. Trevor Etienne, the regular returner, is not with the team right now. On Atlanta, Canales said Kevin Stefanski's offense will likely stay true to its system despite quarterback uncertainty (Tua, Michael Penix Jr., Cooper Rush), since none of them is a dual-threat runner. He said he doesn't see a reason Young has done well in Atlanta, and he wants Young to build on a strong prior week. He praised Xavier Legette's effort, said Legette is part of the game plan, and said Tetairoa McMillan is the focal point of the passing game. Canales flagged Bijan Robinson as a major challenge, calling for discipline, sideline awareness, and team tackling.

title: Ben Johnson excited to be back at Soldier Field in front of Bears fans | Press Conference
headline: Ben Johnson praised Caleb Williams' growing anticipation and decisiveness and said the offense will keep leaning into a heavy run game led by Jonah Jackson and Darnell Wright, with Luther Burden III also singled out for strong film work.
summary: Johnson said the Bears are excited to return to Soldier Field and called the upcoming opponent, a division team on a six-game win streak, a very good and dangerous team. He said that opponent runs the ball at a high rate and has strong perimeter talent, and that its defense forces a lot of fumbles, which Chicago needs to clean up after one last week. He described the defense's blitz-heavy approach, led by Brian Flores, as hard to prepare for, and said the staff has to build answers for it each week. On the run game, he said Jonah Jackson and Darnell Wright are powerful enough that they are hard to stop, and the offense will lean into the right side when matchups call for it while still complementing it to the left. On Caleb Williams, he said the quarterback is playing with more anticipation, is seeing the field well, and got to the right target faster, with a strong week of preparation. Johnson also praised the receivers' work on film, which he showed to the team, and said the offense will keep giving the ball to players who execute most consistently. He was less satisfied with the defense, noting some three-and-outs and good technique but not enough winning performances for championship-level play. He stressed that home wins matter for the season.

title: Zac Taylor Previews Week 2 Against Texans | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Zac Taylor vowed Ja'Marr Chase will see more touches after a quiet Week 1, and praised Mike Gesicki's chemistry with Joe Burrow ahead of the Texans.

He described the game as a must-win in a loud road environment that will require all three phases. On Ja'Marr Chase, Taylor called his lack of targets in Week 1 inexcusable and said the offense would find ways to involve him more, since he impacts games whether he gets the ball behind the line or ten yards downfield. He denied that Chase was used as a decoy, while acknowledging coverage sometimes shifts toward him. Taylor praised Mike Gesicki's route feel and chemistry with Burrow, saying the team trusts him to adjust on the fly. He also said the run game left yards on the table in Week 1 despite a good performance against Tampa's run defense. Taylor expressed respect for C.J. Stroud and Houston's offense, and noted Tampa Bay's strong recent run as a conference rival.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 16th, 2026
headline: Watson keeps the QB1 job for now, and Sampson's IR stint should open the backfield for Raheim Sanders.
summary: Monken said the Browns' Week 1 loss to Jacksonville came down to a poor operation, slow substitutions and cadence issues, plus a defense that could not get off the field after early turnovers. He called the offense's tempo and cadence problems a team-wide responsibility that the staff has been stressing. He said the team will fight to fix it, and that the players have nothing to be down about. He expects Deshaun Watson to play really well against Tampa, but said he doesn't want to look too far ahead and is focused on the midweek practices. On Dylan Sampson's absence, Monken said it opens opportunities for Raheim Sanders and Jay Mack, with Sanders also expected to contribute on special teams. He defended the decision to take the ball first and said the defense played a fair amount of man, despite the zone questions. He said Austin Barber played well as a rookie, though he agreed Barber did not play well enough to keep the starting job if Tevin were healthy. He also said he hopes the whole team, including Jared Verse, takes a big step up in Week 2.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Our Fans Give Us a Huge Advantage | Press Conference
headline: No lineup changes planned for Sunday vs. Washington; Malik Hooker had surgery and DeMarvion Overshown is starting rehab, while Jaishawn Barham is expected to play well at middle linebacker.
summary: Schottenheimer said communication breakdowns from the opener were a team-wide problem, not just linebackers, and that the staff spent meeting time on the keys: be decisive and loud, and make sure calls are received, including with hand signals. He called the errors fixable and said he expects much better communication Sunday, though the home crowd will make it harder. He said there will be no lineup changes or promotions or demotions this week. Malik Hooker had surgery that went well and is moving into rehab, and DeMarvion Overshown is beginning work with the medical staff. He praised T.J. On the middle linebacker spot, he said Jaishawn Barham is smart and will play well whether alongside Dee Winters or Shemar James. He said Tyler Goodson was added as a veteran change-of-pace back with special teams value, and that the staff is still looking at other options to replace Overshown's communication role.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'He's a pro's pro'
headline: Jonnu Smith earned high praise for explosive plays from 13 personnel, Christian Watson drew confidence, and OL Aaron Banks is ramping up toward a return.
summary: LaFleur praised TE Jonnu Smith for his work in the last game, pointing to explosive plays from 13 personnel in both the passing and run game and noting he still has juice in his legs. He called Smith a pro's pro and a model for the locker room. He said Keisean Nixon competed hard during camp and had one of the most complete games of his time in Green Bay. On the running backs, LaFleur said Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd didn't get many carries (about 20 total), and the way to earn more is staying ahead of the sticks and avoiding long downs. He said the team wants a functioning run game because it opens up the passing game, but that the approach depends on the opponent and game situation. He called Christian Watson a player he doesn't worry about, with great energy every day, and said his strong play was no surprise. On the line, Aaron Banks will be back at practice but is still being ramped up, a process that will take the week. LaFleur expects the offensive line to respond well to the film review and said he has enough exposure to the group to trust it. title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts vs. Chiefs
headline: Akeem Davis-Gaither takes the green dot from Camryn Bynum for Week 2 at Kansas City, a communication fix after a rough Week 1.
summary: Steichen said the Colts are moving the green dot (defensive play-calling communicator) from safety Camryn Bynum to linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither for Sunday night at Arrowhead. He framed it as a communication fix: the communication wasn't where it needed to be in Week 1, and the change frees Bynum to direct the secondary while Davis-Gaither handles the middle with the defensive line. He said Davis-Gaither knows the defense well and had some green-dot reps in training camp, and that the team will rotate linebackers, so only one player wears the dot. He called Week 1 a wake-up call but said the team is in a good headspace and needs to move on. On the opponent, he praised Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City's running game, with Kenneth Walker III's big Week 1 game a concern, and said the key is tackling and staying disciplined in run fits. He also described Steve Spagnuolo's defense as demanding to prepare for because of its multiple looks and pressure packages. Steichen said the Chiefs' loud home crowd will be simulated at practice to prepare for communication challenges. On CJ Allen, he said development varies and Allen is still learning, so he'll keep working him in practice before increasing his role.

title: Liam Coen on Prep for Mile High Atmosphere, Building Consistency in Week 2 | Press Conference
headline: Coen praised Trevor Lawrence's Week 1 play and said Travis Hunter's touches could rise as he returns from injury, while BJ Greene is on IR for a couple of weeks.

He said the team has lots of film on Denver from last year and expects a well-coached, talented opponent to play its best. He credited Kansas City's run-heavy approach against Denver with forcing missed tackles, and said the Jaguars want to find balance on offense. He praised Trevor Lawrence's left-side throwing and his Week 1 turnover-free game, saying he used his legs and should be allowed to play freely. He called Travon Walker a disruptive pass rusher who can be a "savage" and said he was pleased to see that show up in Week 1. Coen said Travis Hunter's role could grow as he works back from injury, depending on what gives the team the best chance to win. He announced that BJ Greene, who was hurt on the first play of the game, is going on IR and will be out a couple of weeks. He also said a player brought back to the active roster will help on special teams and at linebacker. Coen framed the road-heavy schedule as something to address openly, with leadership and the captains helping the group handle it.

He described Maxx Crosby as a relentless, disruptive player who has earned league-wide respect. Harbaugh said there is clear opportunity for Brenen Thompson given the injuries in the receiver room, and he praised Thompson's mental and physical approach. On Justin Herbert, he said the sky is the limit and that the team keeps building around him, while conceding the team has not yet reached postseason success. He said Herbert played as well as the situation allowed in the Sunday loss, and that poor second-half offense was a mix of quarterback and team factors. On Kirk Cousins, he expressed deep respect for his mental approach, physical ability, and toughness. When asked about the team ranking last in yards before contact, he deflected to the team working to improve, and he said he has never been satisfied with anything related to football.

title: Kevin O'Connell on Preparing for Bears, Kyler Murray, Injury Updates, Dallas Turner's Progression
headline: Jordan Mason is out about four weeks with a thumb fracture, which should expand DeeJay Dallas's role; Kyler Murray is limited but not ruled out, and Aaron Jones remains the lead back.

He said Jordan Mason has a small thumb fracture that has already been surgically fixed, and that he is expected to be out only a short stint on IR, roughly four weeks. DeeJay Dallas will be activated to replace him, and O'Connell said Dallas will probably see a larger role because of it. Jerome Ford was signed to the practice squad, and O'Connell said the staff will decide game-day status for other backs later in the week. Kyler Murray practiced in a limited capacity under the medical protocol, and O'Connell said he is not ruled out but will be taken day by day, with Friday a key checkpoint for clearance. Jauan Jennings did not practice due to a personal family matter. On the backfield, O'Connell said Aaron Jones will be heavily involved in the lead back rotation, while the staff wants to keep him fresh and use other backs in carries and third-down situations. He also described the Bears defense under Dennis Allen as physical up front, aggressive blitzing, and sticky in coverage, and he praised Caleb Williams as a unique talent who is dangerous both on schedule and off script. Finally, he gave a glowing assessment of Dallas Turner's development, crediting his offseason work, comfort in the scheme, and growing impact.

headline: Pat Freiermuth is a featured piece of the passing game, and McCarthy admitted Darnell Washington needs more touches.

On Week 2 prep, he said Wednesday is the opponent day for the Patriots, and the staff is installing base and third-down calls while reviewing what worked against Atlanta, with only one game of film available for both teams. He acknowledged the downfield throws were missed connections and said the focus is timing, coordination and protection, along with contested catches, while he is still committed to the full menu of short, intermediate and deep throws. He praised Aaron Rodgers, who is 42, for still throwing the ball very well.
